assumptions.text: Possibility judgments can change over time based on new reflection.
The speaker has sufficient cognitive access to their own mental state to report shifts in belief.
The listener will interpret hesitation and repetition as signs of uncertainty rather than indecision.
It is acceptable to revise one's position without implying contradiction.

turn_text: I got you that, Sam. That's Polo. I'm Joe. We're back tomorrow. Have a good night.

explicit_propositions.text: I provided something for you.
The speaker identifies as Joe.
The person being addressed is named Sam.
The entity referred to as 'Polo' is present or relevant.
A future interaction is expected tomorrow.

assumptions.text: Sam recognizes the reference to 'Polo' as meaningful.
The speaker has agency in delivering or referring to 'that'.
The listener trusts the speaker's identification of self and others.
It is appropriate to use informal address ('you', 'we') without formal introduction.
The concept of 'tomorrow' is shared by both parties.
